item.title: Israel’s demand for personal data on Palestinians working for Gaza NGOs is a disgrace
item.description: Israel's intelligence services already maintain extensive knowledge of who works for these NGOs. The new registration requirements appear designed primarily to demonstrate control, writes the former EU representative to Gaza and the West Bank.

item.title: Chernobyl 40 years on — what did we learn?
item.description: As 2026 marks the 40th anniversary of Chernobyl, commemorating it as a historical aberration allows Europe to move on without reckoning. Treating it as a warning about the limits of nuclear governance would require something harder: political humility.

item.title: Do we really need a European alternative to Visa and Mastercard? These are the misunderstandings
item.description: Europe’s push for an “Airbus of payments” reflects real fears of foreign control, but the political discourse is not getting the diagnosis right. True sovereignty lies not in replacing Visa and Mastercard, but in fostering interoperable European alternatives that compete, writes Judith Arnal.

item.title: Child-like sex doll sales spark EU investigation into Shein
item.description: E-commerce giant Shein will be investigated by the European Commission for potential violations of the Digital Services Act for potentially illegal products, addictive design, and transparency violations.

item.title: Gibraltar to regain freedom of movement within days, in post-Brexit legal tidy-up
item.description: The EU Commission has tabled the law on Gibraltar's legal status, giving the Rock's citizens free movement.

item.title: EU top court new search tool dubbed a ‘disaster’ by lawyers
item.description: What was announced as a ‘new gateway to European justice’ has law scholars and professionals up in arms about their ability to conduct research effectively, and potentially “de-democratising access to public data, fuelling an industry of commercial actors”.

item.title: Gay Pride organiser faces jail as Hungary tightens grip on civil rights
item.description: It is the first known case in the EU where a human-rights defender faces imprisonment for organising a Pride march, according to civil society.

item.title: Spain seeks probe into AI-generated child sexual abuse on TikTok, X and Meta
item.description: Spain’s government has asked its public prosecutor on Tuesday to investigate TikTok, X, and Meta for potentially spreading AI-generated child sexual abuse material on their platforms.

item.title: Listen: Could EU migration policy lead to ICE-style raids?
item.description: The EU is readying new rules to speed up deportations of irregular migrants — but dozens of NGOs warn the measures could mirror hard-line tactics used by US immigration authorities. Is Europe about to take a tougher turn on migration?

item.title: Leaked details of what will be in Brussels’ new ‘Made in Europe’ rules
item.description: The European Commission is planning to introduce “Made in EU” requirements across a wide range of strategic sectors, from chips, cars, and chemicals to quantum technologies and renewable energy.
